content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early periods, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes near the end of the history often trigger a sharp price rebound, indicating sentiment-driven momentum.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias when true outcomes dip below historical averages, suggesting underestimation of volatility.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish, as models avoid over-optimism.", "Lagging sentiment indicators correlate with forecast overshoots, suggesting delayed reaction to market signals.", "Models exhibit persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is uniformly positive, indicating sentiment amplification.", "True outcomes frequently deviate from forecasts in the first 5 days, highlighting forecast lag and sensitivity to short-term volatility.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in forecasting when price volatility exceeds historical norms."]}
